target_description: Predicted change (drift) to the next REAL calibration campaign for the same instrument. target_next_valeur_reference is always the next REAL chronological observation - synthetic rows never redefine it.
prediction_unit: UNKNOWN / REQUIRES CONFIRMATION - not recorded in the source ILA data.
training_dataset: data/processed/ILA_train_augmente_features.csv (real TRAIN instruments + safe noise-augmented copies only - TEST instruments never included)
cv_strategy_reference: GroupShuffleSplit by instrument (80/20) for train/test; GroupKFold (5-fold, fold-safe augmentation) on TRAIN instruments only for alpha selection.
known_limitations: On this specific instrument-holdout split, real+augmented beat the persistence baseline. Across 10 independent random instrument splits, augmentation beat baseline in only 3/10 cases, and the mean MAE across splits was not lower for real+augmented than for baseline. Consistent with train_v3_augmented.py's and experiments/audit_v3/FINAL_REPORT.md's prior findings: this dataset's real drift signal is small relative to measurement uncertainty at ~30 rows/instrument, and augmentation does not reliably outperform simple persistence. This is reported as-is, not adjusted to look better.

evaluation_metrics_groupkfold.note: This model uses an instrument-holdout train/test split (GroupShuffleSplit), not GroupKFold, as its primary evaluation - key kept as evaluation_metrics_groupkfold for schema compatibility with src/api/services/prediction_service.py, which reads this exact path for the beats_baseline gate.
evaluation_metrics_groupkfold.beats_baseline_honest_note: Set to False (not the single-split result) because a 10-independent-split robustness check found augmentation beats the persistence baseline in only 3/10 cases and does not reliably outperform it on average - see reports/quality/v4_robustness_across_seeds.csv. The single held-out split above happened to favor augmentation, but that is not treated as the deployable claim.
